questions.prompt: What is the ICD-11 code for a Single Episode of Major Depressive Disorder, Moderate?
questions.explanation: ICD-11 uses 6A71 for Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode. The fourth character specifies severity: .0 for mild, .1 for moderate, .2 for severe.
questions.clinicalPearl: Unlike DSM-5, ICD-11 explicitly codes severity in the main alphanumeric string. Remember: 6A71 = MDD Single, 6A72 = MDD Recurrent.

questions.prompt: Provide the DSM-5-TR code for Panic Disorder.
questions.explanation: Panic Disorder is coded 300.01 in DSM-5-TR and 6B01 in ICD-11. Both require recurrent unexpected panic attacks.
questions.clinicalPearl: Requires recurrent unexpected panic attacks AND at least one month of concern about additional attacks or maladaptive behavioral changes.

vignette.chiefComplaint: The voices won't stop telling me I'm in danger.
vignette.history: 23-year-old male with 6-month history of auditory hallucinations, delusions of persecution, and social withdrawal. No substance use.
vignette.mentalStatus: Disheveled appearance. Responding to internal stimuli. Delusional beliefs about government surveillance.
vignette.duration: Symptoms present for 8 months with continuous signs of disturbance.

questions.explanation: Two or more Criterion A symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, grossly disorganized behavior, negative symptoms) for 6+ months with functional decline.
questions.clinicalPearl: Key differentiator: Schizophrenia requires 6+ months; Schizophreniform is 1-6 months; Brief Psychotic Disorder is <1 month.

questions.prompt: What is the ICD-11 code for Bipolar I Disorder, Current Episode Manic?
questions.explanation: ICD-11 uses 6A60 for Bipolar I Disorder. Specifiers are added for current episode type.
questions.clinicalPearl: Bipolar I requires at least ONE manic episode. Depressive episodes are common but not required for diagnosis.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I can't stop thinking about the accident. I avoid driving now.
vignette.history: 35-year-old female involved in serious car crash 3 months ago. Experiences flashbacks and nightmares.
vignette.mentalStatus: Anxious, hypervigilant, startles easily. Avoids discussion of trauma and driving.
vignette.duration: Symptoms began 2 weeks after accident and persist for 3 months causing significant impairment.

questions.explanation: PTSD requires exposure to actual/threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence with intrusion, avoidance, negative cognitions/mood, and arousal symptoms lasting >1 month.
questions.clinicalPearl: Acute Stress Disorder is 3 days to 1 month post-trauma; PTSD is diagnosed AFTER 1 month. Both share similar symptom clusters.

questions.prompt: Enter the DSM-5-TR code for Autism Spectrum Disorder.
questions.explanation: Autism Spectrum Disorder is 299.00 in DSM-5-TR and 6A02 in ICD-11. Both require deficits in social communication and restricted/repetitive behaviors.
questions.clinicalPearl: DSM-5 consolidated Autistic Disorder, Asperger's Disorder, Childhood Disintegrative Disorder, and PDD-NOS into single ASD diagnosis with severity specifiers.

questions.prompt: What is the ICD-11 code for Borderline Personality Disorder?
questions.explanation: ICD-11 uses 6D10 for Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder, Borderline Type. This represents a major shift from categorical to dimensional approach.
questions.clinicalPearl: ICD-11 reformed personality disorder classification: First assess severity (mild/moderate/severe), then specify trait domains (negative affectivity, detachment, etc.).

vignette.chiefComplaint: I know I'm too thin but I still feel fat when I look in the mirror.
vignette.history: 19-year-old female with BMI of 15. Restricts food intake to <500 cal/day, exercises 3 hours daily.
vignette.mentalStatus: Preoccupied with weight and calories. Intense fear of gaining weight. Distorted body image.
vignette.duration: Significant weight loss (25 lbs) over 8 months. Amenorrhea for 4 months.

questions.explanation: Anorexia Nervosa requires: restriction leading to low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight, and disturbed body image. BMI <18.5 in adults.
questions.clinicalPearl: Key difference from Bulimia: Anorexia involves restrictive behavior without regular binge-purge cycles. Specifier: restricting type vs. binge-eating/purging type.

questions.prompt: What is the DSM-5-TR code for Alcohol Use Disorder, Moderate?
questions.explanation: Alcohol Use Disorder is 305.00 in DSM-5-TR for mild/moderate severity. Severity: Mild (2-3 criteria), Moderate (4-5), Severe (6+).
questions.clinicalPearl: DSM-5 merged alcohol abuse and dependence into single Use Disorder continuum. ICD-11 uses 6C40 with fourth character for severity.

questions.prompt: Provide the ICD-11 code for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
questions.explanation: OCD is 6B20 in ICD-11 and 300.3 in DSM-5-TR. Characterized by obsessions and/or compulsions causing distress/impairment.
questions.clinicalPearl: ICD-11 moved OCD from Anxiety Disorders to new 'Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders' chapter, reflecting distinct neurobiology.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I keep forgetting where I put things and getting lost in familiar places.
vignette.history: 72-year-old male with progressive memory decline over 2 years. Difficulty managing finances and medications.
vignette.mentalStatus: MMSE score 22/30. Impaired recent memory, word-finding difficulties. Preserved remote memory.
vignette.duration: Gradual onset over 2 years with steady progression affecting ADLs.

options: Major Neurocognitive Disorder due to Alzheimer's Disease
questions.answer: Major Neurocognitive Disorder due to Alzheimer's Disease
questions.explanation: Major NCD requires significant cognitive decline interfering with independence. Alzheimer's is most common etiology with insidious onset and gradual progression.
questions.clinicalPearl: Mild NCD: modest decline, independence maintained. Major NCD: significant decline, independence compromised. MMSE <24 suggests major NCD.

questions.prompt: What is the DSM-5-TR code for Insomnia Disorder?
questions.explanation: Insomnia Disorder is 307.42 in DSM-5-TR and 7A00 in ICD-11. Requires difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep ≥3 nights/week for ≥3 months.
questions.clinicalPearl: Must cause significant distress/impairment and occur despite adequate opportunity for sleep. Rule out other sleep disorders first.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I found myself in a different city with no memory of how I got there.
vignette.history: 28-year-old female with history of childhood trauma. Episodes of 'losing time' and finding unfamiliar items in possession.
vignette.mentalStatus: Alert but confused about recent events. No neurological findings. Appears distressed.
vignette.duration: Recurrent episodes over 6 months following stressors.

questions.explanation: Dissociative Fugue involves sudden unexpected travel away from home with inability to recall past and confusion about identity.
questions.clinicalPearl: In DSM-5, fugue is specified as 'with dissociative fugue' under Dissociative Amnesia. ICD-11 codes it separately as 6B64.

questions.prompt: Provide the ICD-11 code for Somatic Symptom Disorder.
questions.explanation: Somatic Symptom Disorder is 6C20 in ICD-11 and 300.82 in DSM-5-TR. Requires one+ somatic symptoms causing distress/disruption with excessive thoughts/feelings/behaviors.
questions.clinicalPearl: Key change from Somatization Disorder: focus is on DISTRESS about symptoms, not number of symptoms. Medical explanation may or may not exist.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I've always felt like I was born in the wrong body. I want to transition.
vignette.history: 16-year-old assigned male at birth. Persistent identification as female since age 5. Requests hormone therapy.
vignette.mentalStatus: Congruent gender identity as female. Significant distress about secondary sex characteristics. No psychosis.
vignette.duration: Persistent feelings for 11 years causing clinically significant distress.

questions.explanation: Gender Dysphoria requires marked incongruence between experienced and assigned gender for ≥6 months with significant distress/impairment.
questions.clinicalPearl: ICD-11 uses 'Gender Incongruence' (HA60) and moved it from Mental Disorders to 'Conditions Related to Sexual Health' to reduce stigma.

questions.prompt: What is the DSM-5-TR code for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia)?
questions.explanation: Persistent Depressive Disorder is 300.4 in DSM-5-TR and 6A74 in ICD-11. Combines chronic major depression and dysthymic disorder.
questions.clinicalPearl: Requires depressed mood for ≥2 years (≥1 year in children/adolescents) with ≥2 additional symptoms. May have superimposed major depressive episodes.

questions.prompt: Enter the ICD-11 code for Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
questions.explanation: GAD is 6B00 in ICD-11 and 300.02 in DSM-5-TR. Requires excessive anxiety/worry occurring more days than not for ≥6 months.
questions.clinicalPearl: Key feature: difficulty controlling worry. Associated with restlessness, fatigue, concentration problems, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I haven't slept in 4 days but I feel amazing! I'm starting three new businesses.
vignette.history: 31-year-old male with elevated mood, grandiosity, pressured speech, and reckless spending for 10 days.
vignette.mentalStatus: Euphoric mood. Flight of ideas. Psychomotor agitation. No psychotic features.
vignette.duration: Acute onset 10 days ago with significant functional impairment requiring hospitalization.

questions.explanation: Manic Episode requires abnormally elevated/expansive/irritable mood for ≥1 week (or any duration if hospitalized) with ≥3 DIGFAST symptoms causing marked impairment.
questions.clinicalPearl: Hypomania: ≥4 days, NO marked impairment, NO hospitalization. Mania: ≥1 week OR hospitalization, WITH marked impairment. This distinction determines Bipolar I vs II.

questions.prompt: What is the ICD-11 code for Complex PTSD?
questions.explanation: Complex PTSD is 6B41 in ICD-11. Includes core PTSD symptoms PLUS disturbances in self-organization (affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, interpersonal difficulties).
questions.clinicalPearl: ICD-11 recognizes CPTSD as distinct from PTSD. DSM-5-TR does NOT include CPTSD as separate diagnosis (symptoms captured under PTSD + comorbidities).

questions.prompt: Provide the DSM-5-TR code for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Presentation.
questions.explanation: ADHD Combined Presentation is 314.01 in DSM-5-TR and 6A05 in ICD-11. Requires ≥6 symptoms of inattention AND ≥6 symptoms of hyperactivity-impulsivity.
questions.clinicalPearl: Presentations: Combined (314.01), Predominantly Inattentive (314.00), Predominantly Hyperactive-Impulsive (314.01). Onset before age 12. Symptoms in ≥2 settings.

vignette.chiefComplaint: Everyone abandons me. I hate being alone but I push people away.
vignette.history: 24-year-old female with unstable relationships, self-harm, emotional lability, and chronic emptiness.
vignette.mentalStatus: Intense affect. Fear of abandonment. Splitting (idealization/devaluation). Impulsive behaviors.
vignette.duration: Pattern evident since adolescence across multiple contexts.

questions.explanation: BPD requires ≥5 of: frantic efforts to avoid abandonment, unstable relationships, identity disturbance, impulsivity, suicidality, affective instability, emptiness, anger, paranoia/dissociation.
questions.clinicalPearl: Mnemonic: AM SUICIDE - Abandonment, Mood swings, Suicidality, Unstable relationships, Impulsivity, Chronic emptiness, Identity disturbance, Disassociation, Explosive anger.

questions.prompt: What is the DSM-5-TR code for Body Dysmorphic Disorder?
questions.explanation: Body Dysmorphic Disorder is 300.7 in DSM-5-TR and 6B21 in ICD-11. Preoccupation with perceived defects/flaws in physical appearance not observable to others.
questions.clinicalPearl: Specifier: with muscle dysmorphia. Insight specifier: good/fair, poor, absent/delusional. Repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, seeking reassurance) required.

questions.prompt: Enter the ICD-11 code for Binge-Eating Disorder.
questions.explanation: BED is 6B82 in ICD-11 and 307.51 in DSM-5-TR. Recurrent binge eating with loss of control, marked distress, ≥1/week for 3 months WITHOUT compensatory behaviors.
questions.clinicalPearl: Key difference from Bulimia: BED has NO regular compensatory behaviors (purging, fasting, excessive exercise). Most common eating disorder in US.

vignette.chiefComplaint: I need it every day now. I've tried to quit but I shake all over.
vignette.history: 45-year-old male drinking 1L vodka daily for 5 years. Multiple failed quit attempts. Lost job due to drinking.
vignette.mentalStatus: Mild tremor. Elevated GGT. Reports tolerance and withdrawal. Continues despite health/social consequences.
vignette.duration: Pattern escalating over 5 years with physical dependence developed.

questions.explanation: AUD Severe requires ≥6 of 11 criteria: impaired control, social impairment, risky use, pharmacological criteria (tolerance/withdrawal).
questions.clinicalPearl: DSM-5 severity: Mild (2-3), Moderate (4-5), Severe (6+). ICD-11: 6C40.0 (single episode), 6C40.1 (harmful pattern), 6C40.2 (dependence).

questions.prompt: What is the DSM-5-TR code for Narcolepsy?
questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is 347 in DSM-5-TR and 7A24 in ICD-11. Requires recurrent sleep attacks ≥3/month for ≥3 months with cataplexy and/or low CSF hypocretin-1.
questions.clinicalPearl: Type 1: with cataplexy OR low hypocretin. Type 2: without cataplexy, normal hypocretin. Tetrad: Excessive daytime sleepiness, Cataplexy, Sleep paralysis, Hypnagogic hallucinations.
